signals.topic: How dogs understand us — cognition science
signals.summary: A cluster of new research on canine communication — that breeding and training both shape how dogs read human cues — landing across science desks within a day.
signals.why_now: Three independent outlets inside 24h: earth.com 'Is a dog's talent for listening born or trained?' (11h), The Brighter Side 'Generations of breeding changed how dogs' brains process human communication' (14h) and Phys.org 'Both breeding and training influence dogs' capacity for communication' (20h). Genuinely multi-source; producible as candid dog portraits, though the underlying story is text-led.

signals.summary: Evergreen feline-behaviour explainers — why cats sit on laptops, get the zoomies, head-rub and 'act nice' — a reliably high-engagement, endlessly renewable cat format.
signals.why_now: A steady multi-outlet run: BBC Science Focus 'Why your cat loves sitting on your laptop', Indian Express 'Why your cat sits on your laptop', PetMD 'Why Do Cats Get the Zoomies?' and NYT 'Your Cat Is Being Nice? Think Again.' Producible as cats in domestic scenes.

signals.summary: The wellness industry moving into pet care — supplements, at-home health testing, longevity routines — as pet humanisation deepens.
signals.why_now: ZME Science 'Poochmaxxing: the wellness industry is coming for your pets' (26h) and Trend Hunter 'At-Home Pet Health Testing Kits' (12h), against a steady backdrop of pet-humanisation trend pieces. Producible via pets with wellness props and calm home settings.

signals.summary: The 'catio' — enclosed outdoor patios that let indoor cats safely be outside — as a durable pet-DIY and design crossover.
signals.why_now: CBC 'Why catios are great for your cat's well-being — and how to build one' and Brooklyn Paper 'One Brooklyn cat owner's catio reflects growing pet care trend', supported by 'Outdoor Access May Benefit Cats' research. Older but evergreen, and cleanly producible as a built exterior scene.
